title: Forever Add-on Catalog
description: The add-ons Forever Add-on Manager can find and install, for every edition of the game, and their authors. Generated by scripts/generate.cs from the add-ons whose releases passed the release check, plus the hand corrections in overrides/. Rules the schema can't express (unique IDs, references between entries and to authors, folders claimed twice, author profiles) are checked by scripts/validate.cs.

$schema.description: Optional link to this schema, for editors.

schemaVersion.description: The format version. The app refuses a catalog whose schemaVersion it doesn't know.

version.description: The catalog's own version, bumped whenever entries change, so the app can say what's new.

editions.description: Every edition of the game the catalog covers, keyed by edition ID, in Battle.net's order: names, the live client each was checked against, and how it reads an add-on.

authors.description: Every author an entry names, keyed by a stable author ID (the same rules as add-on IDs).

id.description: Lowercase letters and digits, words joined by single hyphens. Stable: never changed, never reused. Add-on IDs and author IDs follow the same rules.

tag.description: One of the catalog's tags. Adding one is a schema change, so the app can give it an icon at the same time.

folder.description: A top-level AddOns folder. Letters, digits, _ . - and !, and spaces inside: a leading ! makes the game load it first (!BugGrabber). No paths, no leading dot, and no trailing space or dot (Windows drops those).

tocPath.description: The .toc to read the Interface from, relative to the zip's top level, with forward slashes ("Questie_Forever.toc" or "OpenMap/OpenMap.toc").

editionId.description: A fixed edition ID. Adding one is a schema change.

edition.description: One edition of the game. The app takes its names from here, so a new Classic expansion renames an edition without an app update.

of.description: For a PTR: the live edition Battle.net files it under, even when it runs another edition's version. Left out for a live edition.

name.description: Battle.net's name, with (Retail) added to World of Warcraft; a PTR's as Battle.net lists it (PTR (Classic Era)).

shortName.description: For tight places: labels and the edition switcher.

folder.description: The edition's folder in the World of Warcraft folder.

interface.description: The Interface number of gameVersion (1.60.1 gives 16001, 12.1.5 gives 120105).

interfaceSince.description: The day the live client moved to this Interface (YYYY-MM-DD), for the 60 days an add-on not updated for it yet stays listed.

tocSuffixes.description: The .toc suffixes the edition loads, most preferred first: <Folder><suffix>.toc for each in order, then the plain <Folder>.toc. A PTR lists the version it runs.

gameTypes.description: The game type names its [AllowLoadGameType] and [ExcludeLoadGameType] load conditions use.

packagerFlavors.description: The flavors the common packager's release.json gives this edition's files.

fileWords.description: Words in a release file's name that mark it as this edition's.

addonEdition.description: An add-on on one edition: what its latest checked release lists for it.

interface.description: The Interface the release lists for this edition.

upToDate.description: Whether that is the edition's current Interface (checked by scripts/validate.cs).

released.description: The day (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD) that release was published. Left out when it isn't known.

author.description: One author: how they're shown, and their own pages.

name.description: One name: the add-on's main author, or the owner of its listing on its first source. Not a list or a group.

homepage.description: The author's own site, not an add-on's page.

profiles.description: The author's own pages on GitHub, Wago and CurseForge, as each site writes them: at most one per site (checked by scripts/validate.cs).

sponsor.description: Every page where the author asks for support, as the author lists them, most preferred first: their GitHub Sponsors page, the links in FUNDING.yml, the Donate button on their CurseForge or Wago page, then the other support links they list there. Left out when the author lists none.

repo.description: owner/name. The release GitHub flags as Latest is used, never a pre-release.

assetPattern.description: Regular expression (.NET) the release asset's file name must match.

excludePattern.description: Regular expression (.NET) for asset names to skip even when assetPattern matches.

downloadPage.description: The page where the player downloads the Forever release by hand: the project's files page, filtered to the right game version when CurseForge allows it. Only when the project's front page would lead to the wrong file.

downloadHint.description: How to recognise the Forever download on that page, for the player ("the file whose name ends in -forever"). Only when the page alone doesn't make it clear.

downloadPage.description: The page where the player downloads the Forever release by hand: the add-on's versions page, filtered to the right game version when Wago allows it. Only when the add-on's front page would lead to the wrong file.

downloadHint.description: How to recognise the Forever download on that page, for the player ("the file whose name ends in -forever"). Only when the page alone doesn't make it clear.

withdrawn.description: A release the app never offers.

release.description: The release as the source names it: a GitHub tag, a CurseForge file ID or a Wago release.

override.description: Changes that apply from a given release on, for when an add-on adds or renames a folder or moves its .toc.

homepage.description: Only when the add-on's own page isn't the default: its repository, else its first source's page.

repository.description: The public GitHub or GitLab repository that holds the add-on's source code, whatever its licence. Never one that only hosts issues. Left out when the code isn't public.

issues.description: Where players report problems to the author: the repository's issues when it has them turned on, else the tracker the author links from their CurseForge or Wago page. Left out when there isn't a working one.

from.description: Where the generator took each value from, so a wrong one is easy to trace and fix.

entry.description: The whole entry is an override: the add-on isn't released on GitHub.

author.description: The ID of its author in "authors".

summary.description: One line for lists and cards, from the author: the main .toc's Notes, else the repository's description, else its README's first sentence, else an override. Cleaned of colour codes and textures, and cut to about 120 characters.

summaries.description: The summary in other languages, from the .toc's Notes-xxXX lines, keyed by the game's locale (deDE, frFR ...).

tags.description: From the fixed list (schema/README.md). The first is the add-on's main tag: the app shows its icon when the add-on has none.

added.description: The day the entry joined the catalog (YYYY-MM-DD), for sorting by date added. Optional in the format, but the validator requires it on a new entry in a PR.

icon.description: A small square PNG: the main .toc's IconTexture when it's one of the add-on's own files (never game art), converted and kept in this repo's icons/, or an override. Left out otherwise; the app shows its main tag's icon.

editions.description: The editions it supports, keyed by edition ID, each with the Interface its latest checked release lists. Written by the catalog's generator.

requires.description: Catalog IDs that must be installed too.

optional.description: Catalog IDs it works with when they're installed.

conflicts.description: Catalog IDs it overlaps with. A warning, not a blocker.

notes.description: What a player should know before installing, from the add-on's override.
